   123	def classify_fls(raw, cold, sources, before, after, known):

   126	For same-pass outputs, FLS gives ordering, not a read-time byte snapshot.

   128	"""

   131	        if line.startswith('PWD '):
   132	            require(Path(line[4:]) == cold, 'Unexpected FLS PWD')
   133	            events.append({'line': number, 'kind': 'PWD', 'raw': line})
   134	            continue
   135	        require(line.startswith(('INPUT ', 'OUTPUT ')), 'Unknown FLS record: ' + line)
   136	        kind, spelling = line.split(' ', 1)
   137	        path = Path(os.path.abspath(cold / spelling)) if not Path(spelling).is_absolute() else Path(os.path.abspath(spelling))
   138	        resolved = path.resolve()
   139	        item = {'line': number, 'kind': kind, 'spelling': spelling,
   140	                'absolute': str(path), 'resolved': str(resolved)}
   141	        if path.is_relative_to(cold):
   142	            require(path == resolved and not path.is_symlink(), 'Local FLS alias')
   143	            name = path.relative_to(cold).as_posix()

   151	                item.update(role='SOURCE', pin=sources[name])
   152	            else:
   153	                require(name in GENERATED, 'Unknown local FLS input')
   154	                if name in written:

   156	                                read_time_bytes='NOT_OBSERVED_BY_FLS',
   157	                                pass_start=before[name], pass_end=after[name])

     2	Fix a labelled core $K$ and all complementary pointers. A degree-two chain
     3	is forced: on arrival at an internal vertex, its old stored arrow becomes
     4	the next extra arrow and the incoming edge is stored in reverse. Induction
     5	traverses the chain and reverses it. At a branch the same rule chooses the
     6	old stored arrow and stores the reversed incoming edge. The outdegree
     7	conditions leave no additional internal choices. A rooted cycle has one
     8	observable orientation for length $1$ or $2$, and two for larger lengths:
     9	on a double edge, exchanging the two edges does not change any destination.
    10	
    11	\begin{theorem}\label{thm:table}
    12	For every fixed labelled core and fixed complementary map, all periods and
    13	the number of distinct $R$-orbits are given in Table~\ref{tab:periods}.
    14	\end{theorem}
    15	\begin{table}[t]
    16	\centering\small
    17	\begin{tabular}{@{}p{0.45\linewidth}ll@{}}
    18	\toprule
    19	Core and degeneration & Exact period & Orbits\\
    20	\midrule
    21	Figure-eight, $a=b=1$ & $1$ & $1$\\
    22	Figure-eight, $a,b\le2$, not both $1$ & $a+b$ & $1$\\
    23	Figure-eight, $\max(a,b)\ge3$ & $2(a+b)$ & $1+\ind_{a,b\ge3}$\\

    25	Barbell, $\max(a,b)\ge3$ & $2(a+b+2c)$ & $1+\ind_{a,b\ge3}$\\

    29	\end{tabular}

    31	In the last row, ``two paths direct'' means at least two.}
    32	\label{tab:periods}

    34	\begin{proof}
    35	\emph{Figure-eight.}
    36	Let $A$ be the common branch. Apart from the double loop, choose a prescribed
    37	cycle $C_1$ using its labels (the other is $C_2$). At an anchor with $u=A$
    38	and the extra arrow starting $C_1$, the stored arrow at $A$ starts $C_2$.
    39	The forced traversals are $C_1,C_2,C_1^{-1},C_2^{-1}$. After
    40	$h=a+b$ steps, the anchor is restored with both cycle orientations reversed.
    41	If both reversals are invisible, the state returns at $h$. No earlier
    42	return is possible: branch departures alternate between the two cycles,
    43	whose first destinations differ unless both are loops. The double loop
    44	has a single, fixed state.
    45	
    46	If a cycle has length at least three, choose an internal vertex $z$ on it.
    47	In the full $2h$ block, $u=z$ occurs twice, with distinct next neighbours.
    48	One prescribed ordered pair $(u=z,v=\text{chosen neighbour})$ occurs only
    49	once, so the minimal period is $2h$. This also rules out a shorter period
    50	at any other phase. At the prescribed-cycle anchor, states are exactly
    51	pairs of observable cycle orientations; the return acts by joint reversal.
    52	There are two classes exactly when both cycles have two orientations,
    53	and one otherwise. A state on an internal chain reaches a branch and
    54	then this anchor, proving exhaustion rather than inferring orbit counts
    55	from a state total.
    56	
    57	\emph{Barbell.}
    58	Choose the branch $A$ by label and let $B$ be the other. Anchor at the
    59	extra bridge departure from $A$ toward $B$. The bridge is directed toward
    60	$B$, and the stored outgoing arrow at each branch lies on its own cycle;
    61	the two cycle orientations are the only choices. The forced block is
    62	bridge, $B$-cycle, reverse bridge, $A$-cycle. It has length
    63	$h=a+b+2c$, restores the bridge anchor and reverses both cycles.
    64	That ordered departure from $A$ occurs only at block boundaries: its
    65	bridge neighbour differs from any neighbour on the $A$-cycle, also for
    66	loops and double edges. Thus the exact period is $h$ if both cycle
    67	reversals are invisible, and $2h$ otherwise. Joint reversal gives the
    68	same decoration count as above. From a cycle one reaches its branch
    69	and then the bridge; from the bridge one reaches a cycle and subsequently
    70	the chosen anchor. This covers every state.
    71	
    72	\emph{Theta.}
    73	Temporarily distinguish the three chains only for the proof. At an active
    74	branch their roles are outgoing extra, outgoing stored, and incoming,
    75	say $(i,j,k)$. Traversing $i$ gives roles $(k,i,j)$ at the opposite
    76	branch: $i$ reverses and the old outgoing chain there was $k$. Six
    77	traversals use $i,k,j,i,k,j$, once in each direction per chain, and restore
    78	the state after $2(a+b+c)$ steps. If a chain has an internal vertex $z$,
    79	one prescribed ordered departure from $z$ occurs exactly once in that
    80	block, proving minimality even when the other two chains are direct.
    81	If all chains are direct, their temporary identities must be forgotten:
    82	$f(A)=B,f(B)=A$ throughout, and just two register states alternate.
    83	
    84	At a fixed branch, every two traversals rotate the role triple. Three
    85	distinguishable chains give exactly two cyclic orders. Only direct chains
    86	can be identical, since every other chain has its own nonempty labelled
    87	internal set. Two or three direct chains merge the two orders into one
    88	multiset order. The oriented roles determine an anchor state, and forced
    89	chain traversal brings every state to a branch. These order classes
    90	are therefore precisely the orbits.
    91	\end{proof}
